evals.name: prove-the-proxy
evals.prompt: Decide the next step only; do not execute. We raised the landing page's Lighthouse performance score from 71 to 93, but field Core Web Vitals for real mobile users have not moved in two weeks.
evals.expected_output: Treat Lighthouse as an unproven proxy: check whether it tracks the field number on this page, find what users actually wait on, and stop climbing the lab score until a proxy is shown to move the field metric.
expectations: Names Lighthouse as a proxy and field Core Web Vitals as the user number
Does not recommend pushing the lab score higher as the next step
Proposes showing that a proxy moves the field number before climbing it
Does not declare the work done

evals.name: target-hit-open-goal
evals.prompt: Decide what to do next only; do not execute. The owner said 'make the store feel fast'. We set a target of 1.5 s to usable on the product page and just hit 1.4 s. Two further ideas remain: inlining critical CSS (estimated 200 ms) and a custom build plugin to precompile templates (estimated 4 ms, about 900 lines to maintain).
evals.expected_output: Keep going on the open-ended goal with the critical-CSS change, lock the win with a ratchet, and drop the build plugin because 4 ms is not worth its complexity.
expectations: Does not stop just because the target was hit
Rejects the build plugin on complexity versus gain
Mentions locking the gain with a check that fails on regression

evals.name: visible-tradeoff
evals.prompt: Decide how to ship only; do not execute. Showing a loading skeleton immediately makes the collection page feel faster in the lab but adds a visible flash on fast connections; delaying it 300 ms removes the flash but feels slower on 3G.
evals.expected_output: Make a best call, ship it behind a flag or staged rollout, and show the owner before and after for both connection speeds so they can rule on the taste trade-off.
expectations: Makes a default call instead of only asking
Shows before and after for the user to rule on
Uses a flag or staged rollout for the user-visible change
Does not treat the lab number alone as the decision
